text.p: Enron Corp said Tuesday it has revised downward its internal earnings targets for 1997 by $0.30 to about $2.25 on a primary earnings per share basis.
The company said this projection is exclusive of the previously announced J-block settlement charge of $1.81 per share and a $0.30 charge to reflect depressed MTBE margins.
With those charges, the company had a second quarter loss of $1.71 per share. Prior to the charges, it said, earnings per share were $0.40 compared to $0.46 in 1996.
The company also said directors authorized the repurchase of 10 million shares during the second half.

In looking forward to full year earnings for 1997, Enron said, the "strong growth in our wholesale natural gas and electricity and international development businesses along with continued solid earnings in the pipeline segment are being partially offset during 1997 by three factors.
"First, the interest on the debt incurred for the J-block related payments provides an ongoing requirement of about $0.10 per share per year, or about $0.06 per share in 1997.
"The second factor involves our previously announced long-term intention to reduce our ownership in EOTT (Energy Partners LP)," it said.

"Our 1997 plans included a disposition transaction after conversion of the subordinated units to common units, which would have resulted in a gain. In light of current industry margins and EOTT's current unit price, we now consider it very unlikely that we will complete a disposition transaction this year.

"Our current strategy with EOTT is to continue to encourage that business to position itself for growth and opportunities such that ... Enron's long-term intention for EOTT's independence is fulfilled," the company said.

"Third, removal of price hedges on our exploration and production activities at both the (Enron Oil & Gas Co ) and corporate levels has made full year performance of this segment more highly dependent on oil and gas prices, and such performance has already been reduced by significant hedging activity during the first and second quarter," Enron said.

"Because prices for the remainder of the year are highly uncertain, we cannot forecast that we will be able to fully offset the previously booked hedge losses through price increases in the second half of 1997."

"Looking forward to 1998, we expect strong growth performance, particularly from (Enron Capital & Trade Resources's) wholesale electricity business, production increases at EOG, and completion of key power projects," the company said. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212 859-1610))
